name: Diresight
description: Surveil 2. Draw two cards, then you lose 2 life.
assumptions: Read the C (source, owner:me, qty:0..2, --→gy, thing:any) + D (emit, owner:me, thing:library-look) node pair together as a single "Surveil 2" instruction, matching the actions registry's surveil-N template (source qty:0..N→gy plus emit library-look) with N=2 taken from C's qty upper bound, even though C and D are both independent flow roots rather than one node.

Read the automatic (non-stack) chain D→E→F as one continuous printed effect/paragraph (surveil, then draw two, then lose 2 life), since D's `to` field is "--" (not "stack"), so nothing gets priority between the steps -- no real interruption point.

Treated A→B (cast→move to graveyard) as ordinary post-resolution housekeeping (a resolved sorcery going to its owner's graveyard), not itself printed text -- consistent with the same A→B shape seen on other plain sorceries in this dataset.

Treated C/D as roots ungated by A (the cast node) as the schema's normal way of representing a sorcery's own resolution effect (no explicit "spell resolves" trigger node exists in this schema), not as a sign the effect is somehow independent of the spell being cast.
couldNotDerive: Any reminder/flavor text for the surveil keyword action (the registry only encodes its mechanical shape, not printed reminder text).
notes: Confirmed against the real card via forge-model/data/diresight.txt: Diresight, {2}{B} Sorcery, Oracle: "Surveil 2, then draw two cards. You lose 2 life." Forge script: `A:SP$ Surveil | Amount$ 2 | SubAbility$ DBDraw` -> `SVar:DBDraw:DB$ Draw | Defined$ You | NumCards$ 2 | SubAbility$ DBLoseLife` -> `SVar:DBLoseLife:DB$ LoseLife | LifeAmount$ 2`. This lines up exactly with the packet's nodes: C+D (source qty:0..2 to gy + emit library-look) is the Surveil$Amount 2 edge pair, D->E (emit draw qty:2) is DBDraw's NumCards$2, and E->F (emit life-loss qty:2, owner me) is DBLoseLife's LifeAmount$2 targeting the caster (Defined$You). Mana cost {2}{B} and type line Sorcery both match the self registry exactly. No decomposition gap, schema gap, or misinterpretation found -- the blind reconstruction recovered the full three-part sequence (surveil, draw, lose life) with correct owners and quantities on a single attempt. Nothing to flag for a forgeTranslate.ts bug-fixing pass on this card.
